title: Battery Tray Removal and Installation
introduction:
The battery comes out before its tray—think of moving the toolbox before unbolting the shelf. I keep the electrical disconnection, battery hold-down and tray mounting work in that order so the access steps stay clear.

Use the tray illustration to identify the blue component and its magenta mounting bolts. The linked battery procedures below supply the cover, cable and hold-down work needed to reach it, then put everything back.

items.name: Disable remote start
items.detail: If the vehicle has remote start, disable it in the vehicle’s remote-start settings before service. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started during the work, causing personal injury or death.

items.name: Switch off the ignition and remove the key
items.detail: Remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting it during service; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury. On vehicles with engine auto start-stop technology, keep the ignition off when servicing or working near rotating engine parts because the engine may start automatically with the ignition on.

items.name: Wear protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to observe these precautions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Check cooling fans before underhood work
items.detail: With the ignition OFF, inspect all cooling fans for damage, cracks or separation. Do not work under the hood with a damaged fan; have it replaced with a new fan before continuing. A damaged fan can separate during operation and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Disable fans if working nearby
items.detail: Cooling fans can run with the ignition off. If the work brings you near a fan, it must be disabled before you work nearby; unexpected fan operation may cause personal injury. Use the applicable fan-disabling procedure before proceeding near it.

items.name: Control acid and explosive-gas hazards
items.detail: Work in a well-ventilated area. Keep flames, sparks and burning substances away from the battery. Avoid acid contact with skin, eyes or clothing, and shield your eyes against splashes. If acid contacts skin or eyes, immediately flush with water for a minimum of 15 minutes, then get prompt medical attention. If acid is swallowed, call a physician immediately. Failure to observe these precautions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Lift without squeezing the case
items.detail: Lift a plastic-cased battery with a battery carrier or with your hands on opposite corners. Excessive pressure on the end walls can force acid through the vent caps, causing personal injury and/or damage to the vehicle or battery.

items.name: Restore any disconnected vent tube
items.detail: Always properly reconnect the battery vent tube after disconnecting it. Leaving it disconnected could allow harmful gases into the cabin, causing serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Wash after handling
items.detail: Battery posts, terminals and related accessories contain lead and lead components. Wash your hands after handling them; failure to do so may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Fastener tightening and battery handling
items.detail: Have a torque wrench suitable for the tightening specifications given below. A battery carrier is an alternative to lifting with hands on opposite corners.

items.name: Conditional scan-tool requirement
items.detail: If installing a new battery, have a scan tool available for the Battery Monitoring System (BMS) reset after connection.

items.name: Required battery references
items.detail: Use [Battery](#/document/G1692362) and its nested [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356) procedure for battery removal and refitting. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) and the applicable [Battery and Battery Charging Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693181) before starting.

edits.text:
Remove the battery before working on the tray.
Refer to: [Battery](#/document/G1692362) (414-01 Battery, Mounting and Cables, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: The battery occupies the tray, so access begins with the linked Battery procedure and its required [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356) preparation. Remove the retainers and battery cover. Loosen the negative terminal nut and move the negative cable off its post and aside. Then move the positive cable cover aside, loosen its terminal nut and move the positive cable off its post and aside. The negative-only option in the disconnection note is for interrupting vehicle power; removing the battery also requires the positive cable to be disconnected. Next, loosen and remove the battery hold-down bolt and clamp, then lift out the battery using the handling precautions above. I use the supporting drawings to distinguish the cover retainers, cable-clamp nuts and side hold-down: each releases a different part of the access sequence.

edits.text:
Remove the battery-tray bolts shown in magenta, then lift the blue-highlighted tray upward as indicated by the arrow.
Torque on installation: 89 lb.in (10 Nm)
edits.why: With the battery removed, the tray mounting bolts are exposed at its base. The illustration separates the tray fasteners from the surrounding body and suspension hardware; those nearby fasteners are not part of this removal.

edits.text: Install in reverse removal order: refit and secure the tray, then reinstall and connect the battery using the linked battery procedure.
edits.why: Reversing the sequence puts the support back before its load. Refit the tray and tighten its bolts to the specification above. Refit the battery, install its hold-down clamp and bolt, and tighten the hold-down bolt to 71 lb.in (8 Nm). Reverse the cable-disconnection sequence: reconnect the positive cable first, tighten its nut to 44 lb.in (5 Nm), and restore its protective cover; then reconnect the negative cable and tighten its nut to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Refit the battery cover and retainers, and properly reconnect any vent tube that was disconnected. If installing a new battery, use the scan tool to carry out the Battery Monitoring System (BMS) reset after the battery is connected. I finish by checking that the tray, battery hold-down, cable connections and covers are secured. After disconnection and reconnection, some abnormal drive symptoms may occur while the PCM relearns its adaptive strategy; the vehicle may need to be driven to relearn those values.
